label: copy-phase input h fed back early in the copy of a long sequence (recall positions 3-4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the input token is h (100% of activation mass is on in_tok h). Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Within that set it is very sparse: only about 0.5% of copy-phase h inputs activate. Activity is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 79% of mass, L>=8 holds 94%) at recall_idx 3-4 (steps 12-13, i.e. h was original token 2 or 3), where 85% of mass falls. The strongest examples are h at original position 2-3 of an L=9 sequence, often followed by a repeated h or a digit 0. Magnitude is somewhat higher when the token being output at that step is h, 0, w, u, e or b (adding that condition raises precision to about 12% and keeps 67% of mass), but no input-history variable tested separates active from inactive h steps cleanly. So precision stays low and the remaining selectivity is not explained.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=h (+3.17), recall_idx=4 & in_tok=h (+2.56), phase=2 & out_tok=e (+2.55), prev_tok=i (+2.53), phase=2 & out_tok=w (+2.46), recall_idx=3 & in_tok=h (+2.46). Lower it: recall_idx=2 (-1.81), orig8=- (-1.67), recall_idx=1 (-1.53), prev2_tok=o (-1.38).
